instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Supportive Rage
cards.instruction: Remain helpful and encouraging while becoming increasingly furious.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Paint on my sofa. Right, we can fix it. Remember the blotting I taught you? I'll get a cloth.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's on the carpet too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The birthday carpet. Lovely. You're going to get very good at blotting today. Press gently; I'll do this end.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cloth's spreading the color. I need a clean bit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good catch. Finally. Take my clean shirt and keep blotting. I am bloody furious, but you can finish this; I taught you how.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to ask for what you want. Choose your birthday lunch; I'll drive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The seaside place. We'd lose the forty-pound deposit you paid here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Forty pounds. Fine. At least you're finally speaking up. Ring the seaside place; you deserve your choice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've booked it. They want another forty now, and extra for a window table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Eighty before the bloody window. Give me the number. Remember the negotiating I taught you? Ask for the view without the extra; I'll pay the deposit.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Terms and Conditions
cards.instruction: Treat every offer, favor, feeling, and apology as a negotiation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to bargain, so don't look shocked. My ladder costs you two lifts to the station.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need it for five minutes, not a week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're finally naming the quantity. One lift, and you tell your wife my roses have improved.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I just pay five pounds and skip the speech?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nearly a proper offer. Make it six, or keep your five and say we're still friends. I never taught you to leave goodwill out of a deal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you that an apology should cost some effort. I'll forgive the missed birthday if I get first choice of your Christmas visit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum already has Christmas Day.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're finally keeping one promise. Boxing Day, then, and I'll tell her you've made it up to me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want you to mean it, not just tell Mum.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're learning to ask for the full thing. Stay until New Year and I'll mean it. For Boxing Day alone, you get the announcement.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Yes, but My Way
cards.instruction: Agree with others, then reinterpret the agreement entirely in your favor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I'll help move the sofa. I taught you to lift properly; this is a good chance to see what stuck.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then take the other end. It's heavy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. I'll stand at that end and check your knees. You've nearly stopped bending your back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need a second person actually lifting it, not watching.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. Call your brother over; you're ready to show someone else what I taught you. I'll count you both in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course I'll look after your dog during the repairs. I taught you his routine; let's make sure you still remember it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He needs to stay overnight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. Take the guest room, and you can demonstrate breakfast while I have a lie-in.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll stay, but you promised to do his six o'clock walk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I'll see that it's done properly. Set your alarm for half past five. If you remember the lead this time, I won't need to get up.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: The Pattern
cards.instruction: Treat every minor detail as evidence of a much larger problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two office biscuits missing. I taught you to look beyond the obvious: someone is testing how much they can take.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was me. I skipped lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you can identify the immediate cause now. Why is this office keeping trained staff too busy to eat?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody kept me. I forgot because I was watching a video.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nearly there. Check who sent it, like I taught you. If they can choose when you eat, biscuits are the least of this office's problems.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nobody got my meeting email. I taught you to spot a broken chain; this office has stopped communicating.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You left it in drafts. I can see it on your screen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, the screen-checking lesson stuck. But why does everyone's information depend on one person remembering Send?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send it. Go and get your lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're finally taking responsibility. Now you're running communications while I'm absent. Before I go, let me teach you how to choose your successor.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Could You Just…
cards.instruction: Turn a difficult task into tiny favors until the help quietly becomes most of the task.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you hold this shelf bracket? I taught you a steadier grip than mine; let's see if you kept it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Briefly. I'm dressed for work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're finally keeping an eye on the time. One turn of that top screw and you can let go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's holding. The other screws are lined up already.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good eye. Just tighten those, then slide the shelf on. I taught you to check your work before leaving it; I'll bring your coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. Could you pinch these bouquet stems together? My wedding ribbon keeps sliding.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got them. You need wire underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Could you twist this bit round, just where your fingers are?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There. That sharp end will snag the dress.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you tuck it in and wind the ribbon over it? One little bow would hide everything. I'll hold the scissors.
